title.narrative: Provision of Emergency life-saving WASH services to worst drought affected populations in Jowhar District, Middle Shabelle Region, Somalia

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="font-size: 11pt"gtThe project aims at providing emergency life-saving WASH services to the most vulnerable 12000 persons (4992 women, 4608 men, 1200 boys and 1200 girls including PWDs) particularly rural communities and drought displaced persons including those with disabilities and the elderly in Jowhar District, Middle Shabelle Region Somalia that has been seriously affected by impacts of current devastating drought that has compromised existing limited WASH infrastructures and services thus impacting to water availability and quality and exposing the vulnerable populations to dangers of an outbreak of AWD/cholera and other sanitation and hygiene-related diseases. The situation is exacerbated by the likelihood of below average Gu rains ( April - June) according to current weather forecasts that would impact to unprecedented sixth consecutive below average rainfall that will prolong extreme drought conditions and impact further to water crisis situation in 2023. Of particular concern are the increasing number of drought and conflict displaced populations particularly those affected by community and Government-backed offensive against Alshabab Insurgent group in parts of Hirshabelle and Galmudug state thus overstretching existing water services and compromising available sanitation facilities besides worsening the environmental sanitation conditions. lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltpgtThe project is planned for implementation of the following activities:ltbrgt ltspan style="color: black"gt1. Water: lt/spangtltbrgt ltfont color="#000000"gt Rehabilitation of two strategic boreholes in Jameco and Keysanay villages in Jowhar. Rehabilitation work will involve replacing the faulty pumping systems/ submersible pumps, fixing dilapidated elevated water tanks, animal troughs/ goat/sheep and Carmel as well as water points and replacing faulty generators. lt/fontgtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="color: black"gt Upgrade of 10 shallow wells in the following villages: ltspan style="font-family: Arial,"gt(1 in Bayaxaw, 2 in Jowhar Somali, 1 in Caseer, 1 in Nuukaay, 1 in Halgan, 1 in Damasho, 1 Mayuungaale, 1 Blageesaale and 1 Bula Bacaad)lt/spangt
lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="color: black"gt Training of water committee members to manage and maintain the rehabilitated water systems and upgrades shallow wells (ltspan style="font-family: Arial,"gtTraining of 76 Water Committee members (8 per Boreholes *2=16 and 6 per shallow well*10 =60lt/spangt)ltbrgtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltspan style="font-size: 11pt"gt2. Hygiene Promotion:lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="font-size:11.0pt font-family:"gt ltspan style="color:black"gt Zamzam will train 26 community hygiene promotors, on best practices of hygiene and sanitation to conduct comprehensive Hygiene Promotion awareness campaigns to reach 9000 persons including 3456 men, 3744 women, and 1800 children (900 boys and 900 girls ). including PWDs Trained community promoters consisting of women and men will work closely with the community members to highlight their important role in preventing the spread of diarrhea disease at the household and community level and distribute IEC materials translated into the Somali language. Zamzam will coordinate with health and nutrition other implementing agencies working in the district to identify AWD/cholera and malnutrition-affected women and children to distribute 1500 HP kits including MHM (UNICEF will supply from the regional supply hub) to 1500 households who benefited from the water sources rehabilitated to prevent the spread of AWD/cholera and malnutrition rate in Jowhar Districtlt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
